source_text: Accipiens Petrum et duos filios Zebedaei coepit tristari et taediari. Hos ipsos discipulos assumpsit et in monte cum transfigurandus esset. Coepit tristari — multum interest inter tristari et incipere tristari. Tentatus per omnia secundum similitudinem praeter peccatum, non tristatus est tristitia passionis ipsius sed secundum humanam naturam coepit.
thought_title: The beginning of sorrow in Gethsemane
orientation: Origen is commenting on Matthew's account of Jesus taking Peter and the two sons of Zebedee apart in Gethsemane, where he begins to be sorrowful and troubled.
pass_a_gloss: Taking Peter and [the] two sons of Zebedee he began to be saddened and to be wearied. These same disciples he took also on [the] mountain when he was about to be transfigured. He began to be saddened — much [there] is of difference between to be saddened and to begin to be saddened. Tempted through all [things] according to [the] likeness apart from sin, not he was saddened [with the] sadness of [the] passion itself but according to [the] human nature he began.

choices.why: Keeps the emotional state distinct from the onset of it, matching Origen's contrast between tristari and incipere tristari.
Renders the weariness and distress of the Gospel phrase without importing a modern psychological term.
Preserves the inceptive force that Origen immediately makes the center of his argument.
Matches Origen's theological point that the beginning of sorrow belongs to Christ's true humanity, not to the passion itself.

bible_refs.note: Accipiens Petrum et duos filios Zebedaei coepit tristari et taediari
Hos ipsos discipulos assumpsit et in monte cum transfigurandus esset
Tentatus per omnia secundum similitudinem praeter peccatum

pass_b_english: Taking Peter and the two sons of Zebedee, he began to be sorrowful and troubled (Matthew 26:37). These were the very disciples he took with him on the mountain when he was about to be transfigured (Matthew 17:1). He began to be sorrowful—there is a great difference between being sorrowful and beginning to be sorrowful. Tempted in every way according to likeness, apart from sin (Hebrews 4:15), he did not sorrow with the sorrow of the passion itself, but began to according to human nature.

last_rejected.quote: Tempted in every way according to likeness, apart from sin
last_rejected.source_quote: Tentatus per omnia secundum similitudinem praeter peccatum
last_rejected.why: "secundum similitudinem" modifies "tentatus," not "per omnia"; should be "tempted according to likeness in every way" or "in all things."
last_rejected.fix: Tempted according to likeness in every way, apart from sin
last_rejected.ruling: Latin word order is flexible; 'secundum similitudinem' naturally modifies 'tentatus' in English rendering as given.

last_rejected.quote: he did not sorrow with the sorrow of the passion itself
last_rejected.source_quote: non tristatus est tristitia passionis ipsius
last_rejected.why: "tristatus est" is passive/deponent perfect: "he was not made sorrowful" or "he did not become sorrowful," not active "did not sorrow."
last_rejected.fix: he was not made sorrowful by the sorrow of the passion itself
last_rejected.ruling: 'tristatus est' can be stative perfect: 'was sorrowful'; 'did not sorrow' conveys the same meaning adequately.
